Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 42, English)
Life After Death: Karma Redefined, the Pr et Yoni Mechanism, and Why Mantra Shakti Is the Only Real Guarantee

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn satsang r evisiting and deepening the "Life After Death" topic for the benefit of newcomers, gr ounded in Bhaiya's own two years of drishti-verified cases and his guru's dir ect teaching — covering why karma has no inher ent "good/bad" label, what actually happens in the minutes and days after physical death, the specific mechanism by which entities become trapped inside living bodies, and why building personal mantra shakti is the only guarantee this teaching offers, in this life or after it.
1. How This Teaching's "Life After Death" Framework Was Received and Verified

1. Bhaiya states this teaching comes fr om thr ee combined sour ces: his own dir ect experience, what Sri Hanuman Ji Maharaj taught him while under his guru's guidance, and r oughly two years of personally observing and r eviewing actual cases thr ough drishti. 2. Bhaiya candidly admits that when his guru first r evealed this framework, he privately doubted it — wondering whether it might just be his own mind's fabrication ("mann ki ghadant"), a doubt he says naturally arises during intense, repeated personal sadhna. He never voiced this doubt aloud, but states his guru already knew of it regardless, and subsequently showed him direct, live proof — including direct conversations with devtas who work specifically in after -death matters — over the following two years, which fully confirmed what he'd been taught.
2. This Teaching's View of the Garud Puran and Popular Afterlife Stories

1. This teaching states that popular afterlife stories — being fried in oil, specific hellish punishments for specific sins, and so on, as described in the Garud Puran — ar e not literally accurate in the way commonly believed , though it acknowledges the Garud Puran as a puran (a traditional story/scripture) in its own right. 2. This teaching dir ectly states ther e is no Yamraj who arrives after death to weigh a person's good and bad deeds on a cosmic scale and assign them to heaven or hell accordingly .
3. Karma Redefined: No Such Thing as "Good Karma" or "Bad Karma"

1. This teaching's central claim: karma is simply karma — action itself — with no inher ent "good" or "bad" label attached to it. Bhagwan Krishna's teaching in the Gita is described as emphasizing the importance and consequence of karma itself, never categorizing karma into good and bad varieties the way texts like the Garud Puran do. 2. Supporting argument: "good" and "bad" ar e entirely culturally/r egionally defined and ther efor e cannot be universal moral categories — illustrated through several examples: keeping a moustache is considered sinful in some Muslim traditions but a mark of pride/prestige in North India; consanguineous (blood-related) marriage is strictly forbidden in North India but commonly practiced in parts of South India; dietary practices (eating dog meat, snake, or other foods considered taboo in India) are normal or even forced in certain other countries and regions.

3. The conclusion drawn: since "good" and "bad" shift entir ely depending on r egion, cultur e, and perspective, no single, universal ledger of sin and merit could possibly apply consistently to everyone — even something as ordinary as running is considered healthy by some and physically harmful by others, illustrating that every action carries both positive and negative interpretive framings depending on the viewpoint taken. 4. This teaching's own r esolution: since Bhagwan never defined "good karma" and "bad karma" as separate categories, only "karma, and its consequence" is r eal — this insight is described as the moment Bhaiya's own understanding "clicked into place" once his guru explained it this way .
4. What Actually Happens at the Moment of Death

1. This teaching describes each action a person performs in life as generating its own distinct "tattva" (elemental energy signatur e) within the body — coughing generates one tattva, drinking water another , and so on; a person becomes bonded to whichever tattva was most dominant/habitual for them at the time of death. 2. Immediately after death, for roughly five to six minutes, the departed person does not r ealize they have died — they attempt to re-enter their own body or fall back asleep as usual, remaining confused, before roaming nearby for up to about half an hour while becoming increasingly "sookshma" (subtle).
5. The Cremation-Gr ound Ritual and the "Hakini" Passage Mechanism

1. In the Hindu funeral tradition specifically , dung-cakes (uple) ar e burned first at the cr emation gr ound as an offering (bhog) to a r esident authority figur e of that specific cr emation gr ound — described as a kind of local "king" of ghosts who holds jurisdiction there and must be appeased/petitioned before the newly deceased soul, which is frightened and disoriented, can be allowed through. 2. In between this stage and the actual cr emation, a deity called "Hakini" (described as visually r esembling a pr et) uses a ring-shaped device (compar ed to a cir cus hoop a lion jumps thr ough) to move the soul thr ough a specific passage — the ring is described as open at the front and constricted at the back; Hakini gently pushes the soul partway in from the front, then delivers a firm push/"kick" from behind, sending it fully through to the other side. 3. Crucially , this teaching clarifies that passing thr ough this ring does NOT move the soul to a differ ent lok (r ealm) — the person r emains on this same earthly plane (dharti lok). What actually changes is the person's yoni (form/species-class of existence): they instantly take on whatever yoni corresponds to the tattva that was most dominant within them — for most ordinary people, this means becoming a pret. 4. Non-Hindu or non-ritual deaths follow the same underlying mechanism — a sudden or violent death (a road accident, a stabbing) results in the same instantaneous pret-formation on the spot, without any cremation-ground processing, since the same tattva-based transition occurs regardless of ritual.
6. The Bleak, Ignor ed Existence of an Ordinary Pr et

1. This teaching describes the everyday existence of an ordinary pr et as bleak and entir ely unattended — no one offers water , food, or air; no devta or authority checks on them; they simply exist, crying or laughing on their own, largely ignor ed, and ar e described as being, in raw numbers, even mor e numerous than living humans today . 2. The only entities who r eliably interact with pr ets, per this teaching, ar e tantriks — who for cibly contr ol them (illustrated by binding a pr et with a lit bidi/incense to its nose) and compel them to perform tasks, sometimes abusively . A pret can typically only communicate through a tantrik specifically , because the tantrik knows how to "activate" the necessary senses of the human body , described here as a highly capable "device."
7. Why Ancestor (Pitru) Bhog-Offering Practices Originally Began

1. This teaching offers a practical origin story for pitru bhog offerings: newly deceased pr ets, desperate and unattended, try to r each loved ones for help ("listen to me, do this for me") — and out of this dynamic, families began of fering bhog to
appease and communicate with them, which is how some ancestors ended up remaining within the household long-term, occasionally residing inside a specific family member's body .
8. The Detailed Mechanism of Vasana (Lust) Trapping an Entity Inside a Living Body

1. This teaching walks thr ough a specific, extended case-mechanism: a person whose dominant life-tattva was vasana (unfulfilled lust/desire) becomes a pr et carrying that same dominant tattva after death , and — since it was never satisfied physically in life — seeks to satisfy it astrally instead, attempting repeatedly to enter the corresponding body-region (described as "nabhi ke niche," below the navel) of a living person of the opposite sex. 2. Because sensory pleasur e requires physical senses that the pr et no longer has, this r epeated astral "practice" brings the pret no actual satisfaction — yet it continues compulsively anyway . Over time, this creates physical ef fects on the living host: pain and bleeding below the navel in women is specifically attributed to this mechanism. 3. The critical twist: once the pr et succeeds in entering this specific r egion of a living body , it becomes permanently stuck there and cannot leave, even if it wants to — its repeated attempts to exit fail entirely , trapping it in what this teaching describes as a foul, waste-adjacent astral space it must endure continuously , functioning as its own direct punishment (dand) for the original vasana-driven misconduct in life. 4. This teaching frames the overall mechanism as "one arr ow , four targets" (ek teer se chaar nishane): the originally guilty deceased person is punished by permanent entrapment in filth; the living host (who is also stated to carry their own karmic dosh, not to be assumed "pur e" simply because they wer e targeted) suffers physical affliction as a consequence of that same dosh; and both partners in an intimate r elationship suffer declining physical/sexual capacity and weakening emotional bonding as a r esult. 5. A parallel mechanism is described for men: sudden, repeated nightfall (night-pollution) complaints and unexplained weakness/lack of stamina during intimacy ar e attributed to the same r epeated, unsatisfying astral "practice" occurring internally , draining r eal-world sexual capacity over time. This teaching states that, based on Bhaiya's own reviewed cases, roughly 82% involve kaam/vasana as the central underlying issue — describing it as the single most common problem people bring to Ashaeiynn today .
9. Similar Mechanisms for Lobh (Gr eed) and Kr odh (Anger)

1. This teaching describes a parallel case involving lobh (gr eed/attachment): a mother whose excessive attachment to her son leads her , after death, to enter and become permanently lodged inside her son's body — unable to leave, she effectively transfers her own prior life-problems onto her son going forward. 2. A similar pattern is described for krodh (anger)-driven attachment — for example, a mother -in-law's grudge against a daughter -in-law leading to a similarly permanent, un-exitable possession — the underlying principle being that once any negative entity enters a living body this way , it cannot leave on its own; removal requires a specific method that can only be performed through another living human body , since even devtas require a human body to carry out this kind of removal work.
10. This Teaching's View on Black Magic (T antrik Kriya) and "Energy Healing"

1. This teaching states that tantrik kriya (black magic) always r equires a specific "contact" or planted entity alr eady embedded near or within the target — it never occurs as pur e, distant energy alone. This is of fered as a direct critique of practices like tarot reading or reiki healing that claim to remove "negative ener gy" instantly — this teaching states such removals are often illusory , since the underlying entity typically remains embedded, and warns that an inexperienced practitioner risks the embedded entity itself learning and mimicking that same healing technique against them. 2. This teaching explains why tantriks often seem to know a target's plans in advance: a planted pr et near the target can overhear ordinary conversations (e.g., plans to buy a new house) and r eport back to the contr olling tantrik, who then acts pr eemptively . Prets are described as frequently used this way for surveillance/spying purposes by tantriks.
1 1. The Six Enemies (Kaam, Kr odh, Lobh, Mad, Moh, Matsar) as the Root Downward Pull

1. This teaching states that per shastra, the six r oot flaws — kaam (lust), kr odh (anger), lobh (gr eed), mad (pride/intoxication), moh (attachment), and matsar (envy) — ar e all r ooted in agni tattva (fir e element), and ar e specifically what pulls a soul down into a lower yoni after death. 2. A candid caution: this teaching states plainly that no one can simply eliminate these six flaws by sitting in meditation postur e and "r enouncing everything" — describing much of that outward renunciant performance as theatrical ("nautanki"). An illustrative example: great ascetics performing 21-day cave sadhnas can have a witch (chudail) standing behind them the entire time, siphoning of f the very jaap-ener gy they're generating — leaving the ascetic physically depleted (visible dark circles) even as devotees bow at their feet seeking blessings the ascetic can no longer actually give, since the chudail is the one truly receiving that devotion's benefit.
12. Not Everyone Becomes an Ordinary Pr et After Death

1. This teaching clarifies that not everyone who dies becomes a pr et in the way described above — those who have genuinely attained r eal siddhi or tattva-r ealization (for example, a devotee who has attained Hanuman-tattva) ar e instead dir ectly lifted upward by higher powers at the moment of death , bypassing the ordinary pret-formation process entirely . 2. Even while physically alive on earth, however , this teaching states no one truly advances without human mediation of some kind — echoing an earlier teaching's point that even simple things like water are hard to obtain unassisted in the astral world; genuine progress always requires some form of human-body-based support or intervention.
13. Memory and Identity Persist Fully After Death

1. This teaching dir ectly r ejects the popular belief that memory is lost after death — stating instead that a person's full memory (illustratively , chemistry formulas, phone passwords, past relationships) remains completely intact as a pret, exactly as it was during physical life. 2. This teaching offers a specific caution connected to this: an ordinary person calling on "universal energy ," "angels," or similarly vague invoked powers without pr oper spiritual discernment can be answer ed and convincingly "pr oven to" by any nearby entity claiming to be that power — since, as this teaching phrases it, "even a mother -in-law was once a daughter - in-law" — meaning even negative entities were once ordinary humans, fully capable of a convincing, humanlike performance.
14. Devta vs. Devta "Conflict" Is Relative, Not Absolute

1. This teaching explains that what looks like one devta harming or "fighting" another is entirely a matter of r elative perspective: if Hanuman Ji Maharaj is pr otecting one devotee by for cefully suppr essing a second person's attached negativity , this appears as a blessing to the first devotee and as an affliction to the second — while it is, in fact, the same protective action viewed fr om two differ ent positions. 2. This teaching states that devtas/Bhagwan in their true form never literally fight one another — only their subordinate siddhis/shaktis clash on their behalf, with the side possessing gr eater power prevailing. It further notes that increasingly , advanced tantriks now direct devtas themselves (rather than mere prets) to carry out harmful actions — described as considerably harder to counter or reverse, since undoing a devta-level action requires an even greater level of power .
15. Karma, Power , and This Teaching's Cor e Guarantee

1. This teaching r estates its central practical claim: since karma has no inher ent moral dir ection, and "good" or "bad" outcomes ar e ultimately determined by whoever holds mor e power/shakti in a given situation, the only r eliable path to a favorable outcome — in this life or after death — is building one's own personal mantra shakti. 2. A worldly comparison is offer ed: just as ordinary society defers to whoever currently holds political power/authority , regardless of abstract notions of right and wr ong, the astral world operates the same way — power determines outcome, not an inher ent moral scor ecard.

3. Bhaiya's own explicit, limited guarantee: he cannot pr omise that a person's vasana, kr odh, or other flaws will disappear , and he cannot guarantee liberation (moksha) or which specific lok a person will end up in after death. What he can guarantee is that consistent mantra jaap builds real, functioning shakti that makes a person increasingly dif ficult to trouble or exploit — and that even if such a person becomes a pret after death, accumulated mantra shakti ensures they become a "raja" (king) commanding lesser prets, rather than being victimized by them.
16. The Practical Mechanics of Building Pr otection Through Jaap

1. This teaching states that consistent mantra jaap literally builds up pr otective structur es ar ound the body — described here as "12 golas" (twelve spher es) and functioning aura-shielding/chakras — making a person's body substantially harder for any negative entity or ordinary tantrik kriya to penetrate (barring an especially powerful, dedicated tantrik attack). 2. A direct comparison is drawn between spiritual energy-building and modern medicine/nutrition: medicine and supplements ar e described as pr oducing only temporary effects (a dose lasting a few hours, at most a day or two) with no lasting transformation, while sustained mantra shakti compounds and never "fails" or goes to waste. An illustrative live example discussed in this session: an extremely expensive imported nutrition supplement (described as marketed as a topranked product across numerous countries) was examined through drishti and found to primarily function as an astral-ener gy drain rather than a genuine physical remedy — contrasted with the example of a trained commando generating more real ener gy from a single roti than an ordinary person builds in a month.
17. A Caution Against Letting Negativity Interfer e With Intimate Relationships

1. This teaching dir ectly connects the vasana-based possession mechanism (Section 8) to r elationship br eakdown: an entity lodged in the nabhi-niche r egion of one partner directly degrades that person's physical and sexual capacity , damaging couples' intimacy and emotional bonding over time — described as a "third presence" mechanism that this teaching states is frequently the real, unseen cause behind divorces and breakups that otherwise appear to have no clear external cause.
18. Practical Clarifications: The "Tunnel of Light" and Chanting While Traveling

1. Regarding the commonly r eported "tunnel of light" near -death experience, this teaching describes it as a kind of sensory/per ceptual illusion or interface effect experienced during the transition, rather than a literal, objectively r eal physical tunnel. 2. Regarding chanting mantras while traveling or visiting a pilgrimage site (tirtha) away fr om one's usual practice location: this teaching confirms it is entir ely fine and effective to chant anywher e, provided a practitioner does not abandon their spiritual "r oots" (their guru and primary mantra) in the pr ocess — abandoning one's r oots is specifically what causes accumulated energy to fragment or multiply unpr edictably , rather than compound safely over time.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Karma has no inher ent "good" or "bad" label — only karma and its consequence ar e real , since moral categories shift entirely by region and culture (illustrated by moustaches, consanguineous marriage, and dietary norms all being judged oppositely in dif ferent places); popular Garud Puran-style hell stories and Yamraj's judgment scale are described as not literally accurate. At death, a person becomes bonded to whichever "tattva" (elemental energy signatur e) was most dominant/habitual in their life — for roughly five to six minutes after death, the departed doesn't realize they've died, and roams in confusion for up to half an hour before becoming fully subtle. In the Hindu funeral tradition, the deity "Hakini" uses a ring-shaped passage to push the departed soul into its corr esponding yoni — this does NOT change the person's lok (they remain on this same earthly plane); only their yoni/form

changes, based on their dominant tattva — for most people, this means becoming an ordinary pret. Ordinary pr ets exist in a bleak, entir ely unattended state — no food, water , or attention from anyone, more numerous than living humans; only tantriks reliably interact with them, typically by force. Unfulfilled vasana (lust) in life can trap an entity permanently inside a living person's body (nabhi ke niche) — causing physical pain/bleeding, and irreversibly degrading both partners' physical, sexual, and emotional bonding; this teaching attributes roughly 82% of its reviewed cases to vasana-related causes. Similar permanent-possession mechanisms exist for lobh (greed) and krodh (anger)-driven attachment. Any negativity that enters a living body cannot exit on its own — r emoval always r equires a specific method performed through another human body , since even devtas need a human body to carry out this kind of removal. Black magic (tantrik kriya) always r equires a planted "contact" entity near the target — it never works as pur e distant energy alone — this is why instant "negative ener gy removal" claims (tarot, reiki, etc.) are treated skeptically in this teaching, and why some tantriks seem to know tar gets' plans in advance (via planted pret-spies). Devta-vs-devta "conflict" is always r elative to perspective, not literal fighting between true devta forms — only subordinate siddhis/shaktis clash, with the more powerful side winning; advanced tantriks increasingly direct devtas themselves to cause harm, which is far harder to reverse. This teaching's cor e, honest guarantee: it cannot pr omise moksha, a specific afterlife destination, or the disappearance of one's own flaws — but consistent mantra jaap r eliably builds r eal pr otective shakti , making a person harder to exploit in life, and ensuring even a post-death pret existence would be one of relative command ("raja of prets") rather than victimhood. Consistent jaap builds literal pr otective structur es ("12 golas," aura-shielding/chakras) ar ound the body — unlike medicine or supplements, which produce only temporary ef fects, accumulated mantra shakti never fails or goes to waste. The "tunnel of light" near -death experience is a sensory/per ceptual effect, not a literal physical structur e — and chanting mantras while traveling or on pilgrimage is fine anywhere, as long as one doesn't abandon their spiritual "roots" (guru and primary mantra). Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 42, English)
Life After Death: Karma Redefined, the Pr et Yoni Mechanism, and Why Mantra Shakti Is the Only Real Guarantee
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Where does this "Life After Death" teaching actually come fr om? A: Per this teaching, it comes from three combined sources: Bhaiya's own direct experience, what Hanuman Ji Maharaj taught him under his guru's guidance, and roughly two years of personally reviewing actual cases through drishti.

Q2. Did Bhaiya always believe this teaching himself? A: Not immediately — he admits that when his guru first revealed this framework, he privately wondered if it was just his own mind's fabrication, a doubt common during intense sadhna. His guru knew of this doubt regardless and showed him direct, live proof over the following two years, including conversations with devtas who specifically handle after -death matters.

Q3. Are the Garud Puran's descriptions of hell and specific punishments literally accurate? A: No — this teaching states these popular stories aren't literally accurate, while still respecting the Garud Puran as a traditional puran (story/scripture) in its own right.
Q4. Does Yamraj come to judge a person's good and bad deeds after death? A: No — this teaching directly states there is no Yamraj weighing deeds on a cosmic scale to assign heaven or hell.

Q5. Is ther e really such a thing as "good karma" and "bad karma"? A: No — this teaching's central claim is that karma is simply action itself, with no inherent good/bad label. The Gita emphasizes karma and its consequence, but never categorizes karma into good and bad varieties the way texts like the Garud Puran do.

Q6. Why does this teaching r eject a universal good/bad standard for karma? A: Because "good" and "bad" are entirely culturally defined — for example, keeping a moustache is considered sinful in some Muslim traditions but a mark of pride in North India; consanguineous marriage is forbidden in North India but practiced in parts of South India; foods considered taboo in India are normal or even routine in other countries. If morality shifts this much by region, no single universal ledger of sin and merit could apply consistently to everyone.

Q7. So what's this teaching's own r esolution to the karma question? A: Only "karma, and its consequence" is real — Bhagwan never defined separate categories of "good karma" and "bad karma." Bhaiya describes this as the moment his own understanding fully clicked into place, once his guru explained it this way .

Q8. What actually determines what happens to someone right after death? A: Per this teaching, every action generates its own distinct "tattva" (elemental ener gy signature) within the body , and a person becomes bonded to whichever tattva was most dominant/habitual for them at the time of death.

Q9. Does a person r ealize immediately that they've died? A: No — per this teaching, for roughly five to six minutes after death, the departed doesn't realize they've died; they try to re-enter their body or fall back asleep, then roam in confusion for up to about half an
hour while becoming increasingly subtle.

Q10. What actually happens at the cr emation gr ound, per this teaching? A: In the Hindu tradition, dung-cakes are burned first as an of fering (bhog) to a resident authority figure — described as a local "king" of ghosts holding jurisdiction there — who must be appeased before the frightened, disoriented soul can pass through. A deity called "Hakini" then uses a ring-shaped device (like a circus hoop) to push the soul through a passage: a gentle push from the front, then a firm push from behind, sending it fully through to the other side.

Q1 1. Does passing thr ough this ring send the soul to a differ ent realm (lok)? A: No — this teaching is explicit that the person remains on this same earthly plane (dharti lok). What actually changes is their yoni (form) — they instantly take on whatever yoni matches their dominant life-tattva, which for most ordinary people means becoming a pret.

Q12. What happens to someone who dies suddenly or violently , without a pr oper funeral ritual? A: The same underlying mechanism applies — per this teaching, a sudden death (accident, stabbing) results in the same instantaneous pret-formation on the spot, since the tattva-based transition happens regardless of ritual.

Q13. What is daily existence actually like for an ordinary pr et? A: Per this teaching, it's bleak and entirely unattended — no food, water, or air of fered, no devta or authority checking on them; they simply exist, lar gely ignored, and are described as being, in raw numbers, even more numerous today than living humans.

Q14. Who actually interacts with ordinary pr ets? A: Mostly tantriks, per this teaching — who forcibly control them (for example, binding a pret with a lit bidi/incense to its nose) and compel them to perform tasks. A pret typically communicates only through a tantrik, since the tantrik knows how to "activate" the necessary senses of the human body .

Q15. Why did the practice of offering bhog to ancestors (pitru) start in the first place? A: Per this teaching, newly deceased prets, desperate and unattended, try to reach loved ones for help — and families began of fering bhog to appease and communicate with them, which is how some ancestors ended up remaining in the household long-term, occasionally residing inside a specific family member .

Q16. How exactly does unfulfilled lust (vasana) trap an entity inside a living person's body? A: Per this teaching, a person whose dominant life-tattva was vasana becomes a pret carrying that same tattva after death, and — since it was never physically satisfied — attempts repeatedly to satisfy it astrally by entering the corresponding body-region (nabhi ke niche, below the navel) of a living person of the opposite sex.

Q17. Does this astral "practice" actually satisfy the pr et? A: No — per this teaching, sensory pleasure requires physical senses the pret no longer has, so the repeated attempts bring no real satisfaction, yet continue compulsively anyway , causing physical ef fects (pain and bleeding below the navel) in the living host over time.

Q18. Can the pr et leave once it's enter ed this part of a living body? A: No — per this teaching, once it succeeds in entering, it becomes permanently stuck and cannot leave even if it wants to; this entrapment in a foul, waste-adjacent astral space functions as its own direct punishment for the original misconduct.

Q19. Is the living host in this scenario an innocent victim? A: Not necessarily , per this teaching — the living host is also stated to carry their own karmic dosh, which is why they attracted this negativity in the first place; this teaching frames the whole scenario as "one arrow , four tar gets," punishing the deceased, af flicting the host, and weakening both partners' physical and emotional bonding in a relationship.

Q20. Is ther e a similar mechanism affecting men? A: Yes — per this teaching, sudden repeated nightfall complaints and unexplained weakness/lack of stamina during intimacy are attributed to the same repeated, unsatisfying astral "practice" occurring internally , draining real-world sexual capacity over time.

Q21. How common is vasana as the underlying cause in cases Bhaiya r eviews? A: Per this teaching, roughly 82% of reviewed cases involve kaam/vasana as the central issue — described as the single most common problem people bring to Ashaeiynn today .

Q22. Are there similar mechanisms for gr eed or anger , not just lust? A: Yes — this teaching describes a mother whose excessive attachment (lobh) to her son leads her , after death, to become permanently lodged inside her son's body , transferring her own prior problems onto him. A similar pattern is described for krodh (anger)-driven attachment, such as a mother -in-law's grudge against a daughter -in-law .

Q23. Once a negative entity enters someone's body , can it just leave on its own? A: No — per this teaching, once any negativity enters a living body , it cannot exit on its own; removal always requires a specific method performed through another living human body , since even devtas need a human body to carry out this kind of removal work.

Q24. Can black magic work pur ely thr ough distant energy , without physical pr oximity? A: No — per this teaching, tantrik kriya always requires a specific "contact" or planted entity already embedded near or within the tar get; it never occurs as pure, distant ener gy alone.

Q25. Are quick energy-healing methods like tar ot or reiki actually r emoving negative energy? A: This teaching is skeptical — it states such removals are often illusory since the underlying entity typically remains embedded, and warns that an inexperienced practitioner risks the embedded entity itself learning and mimicking that same healing technique against them.

Q26. How do some tantriks seem to know a target's plans in advance? A: Per this teaching, a planted pret near the tar get can overhear ordinary conversations (like plans to buy a new house) and report back to the controlling tantrik, who then acts preemptively — prets are frequently used this way for surveillance/spying.

Q27. What ar e the "six enemies" this teaching r eferences, and what do they do? A: Kaam (lust), krodh (anger), lobh (greed), mad (pride), moh (attachment), and matsar (envy) — per shastra, all rooted in agni tattva (fire element), and specifically what pulls a soul down into a lower yoni after death.

Q28. Can someone eliminate these six flaws just by meditating or renouncing everything outwardly? A: Not necessarily , per this teaching — it states plainly that outward renunciant performance is often theatrical, illustrated by ascetics doing intense cave sadhnas while a witch (chudail) secretly siphons of f their generated jaap-ener gy the entire time, leaving them physically depleted even as devotees seek their blessings.

Q29. Does everyone who dies become an ordinary pr et? A: No — per this teaching, those who have genuinely attained real siddhi or tattva-realization (such as Hanuman-tattva) are instead directly lifted upward by higher powers at the moment of death, bypassing ordinary pret-formation.

Q30. Is memory lost after death, as some people believe? A: No — this teaching directly rejects that belief, stating a person's full memory (illustratively , chemistry formulas, phone passwords, past relationships) remains completely intact as a pret.

Q31. Is it safe to invoke vague things like "universal energy" or "angels" without much spiritual discernment? A: This teaching cautions against it — any nearby entity can claim to be that invoked power and convincingly "prove" itself with signs, since even negative entities were once ordinary humans, fully capable of a convincing, humanlike performance.

Q32. Do devtas actually fight each other , as some stories suggest?
